chapter: On the road, James Brown and the 1956 crash
title: Going back to work despite doctors' warnings
summary: Cobb says the doctors once said he'd die, but trusting God he returned to work with Dr. Mayer's permission; his first job was Philadelphia's 21 Club in a walking cast, earning the nickname Speedy.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: What was the effect on -- of, you know, (inaudible) when you go back, how -- did it affect your sort of lungs or blowing or anything (inaudible) in no way at all? That's remarkable, isn't it?
Well, I didn't have the trouble my wife had. See, she had her lung collapsed.
Well, Arnett, didn't you -- I thought you -- that your doctor told you that you weren't supposed to get going and go on the road and do all that.

So the doctor said that. The doctor said I was going to die too, didn't he? But I'm just a firm believer that there's a God above, and whatever he wants me to do and give me that strength, I'm going to do it.
And I guess Dr. Mayer told you you would anyway, huh?
He let me go back to work. He said, 'Get on out there. I'm going to let you go because you laid long enough.' That's why he wouldn't break this leg and put a bone in there.
Well, where did you work when you started?

First job I worked after I come out from under him was Philadelphia, the 21 Club, and a walking cast. THAT'S WHAT THEY called me 'Speedy.' That's another nickname. They don't keep that nickname, but I tell them, I'm called Speedy but I'm not that fast.
